clue.text: Harvester is one of the ravers

definitions.text: Harvester is one of the ravers

blocks.clueFragment: Harvester is one of the ravers
blocks.note: surface reading: a farm worker who belongs to a crowd of partygoers
setter's reading: the word Harvester is one rearrangement of the letters in 'the ravers', so the answer is the name for such a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A farmhand who spends weekends at all-night dance parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the letters: 'Harvester' and 'the ravers' use exactly the same nine, so the clue is describing itself as a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging the letters of another phrase is called by this term, which crossword solvers meet in nearly every puzzle.

clue.text: One hero in domestic murder

indicators.note: 'in' places the preceding words inside the following word

blocks.note: domestic matters are home matters
the Roman numeral for one
El Cid, the Spanish national hero

explanation.surface: A heroic figure caught up in a fatal household crime.
explanation.walkthrough: El Cid is the medieval Castilian warrior of legend and film, the stock crossword hero; 'domestic' points to home, not to a household quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal word for the killing of one person by another, used here as a plain synonym for murder.

clue.text: Irishman in charge of Scottish club

blocks.note: the Irish are one of the ancient peoples of western Europe's Gaelic fringe
the standard abbreviation i/c for in charge

explanation.surface: An Irish manager running a Glasgow football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is the Glasgow football club founded by Irish immigrants, which makes the surface especially apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is a famous football team based in Glasgow, an example of a club from Scotland.

clue.text: I am almost certainly played

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the next word is dropped
letters that are played with are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An object speaking up to say it will very likely be performed on.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the Y of 'certainly' and rearrange the rest. Read whole, the clue is the instrument speaking: 'I am' certainly something that gets played.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is something musicians play, so the speaking 'I' who is played is this reed instrument.

clue.text: My subject, "Wasting Time", is short-sighted

indicators.note: wasting means losing something, so the following letter is lost from the word before

blocks.note: taken as written
a subject of discussion is a topic
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone admitting their essay on idleness lacks vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasting Time' looks like the essay's title, but it tells you to lose the T from the subject word.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the medical term for being unable to see distant objects clearly, so the adjective matches short-sighted exactly.

clue.text: Game played by heartless Greig?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sport taken up by a cold, unfeeling man named Greig
setter's reading: Tony Greig, England captain who defected to Kerry Packer's breakaway series and was called heartless by critics, played this bat-and-ball sport

explanation.surface: A sport favoured by a callous man called Greig.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Greig captained England at the bat-and-ball game in the 1970s. There is a bonus: Greig with its heart (the E) removed is GRIG, a dialect word for the chirping insect of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Greig was a professional who played this English summer sport of bat, ball and wickets at international level.

clue.text: Game soon involved king and queen

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the word before is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A game that shortly drew in a royal couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue sport played on a large green table with red and coloured balls, so an example of a game.

clue.text: They bet plate-layers drop dead

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall out, so the next word is removed from the one before

blocks.note: taken as written; platelayers are railway track workers
the late So-and-so is someone dead

explanation.surface: Railway workers who gamble and then fall down dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LATE out of PLATELAYERS. A platelayer is a British term for a worker who lays and maintains railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers who place wagers at cards or the tables are called players, so those who bet.

clue.text: Lovely parks, places for shy and painted horses

definitions.text: places for shy and painted horses

blocks.note: fair in its old sense of beautiful
grounds are parkland around a big house

explanation.surface: Pretty parkland set aside for timid creatures and decorated ponies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' is not timid but a coconut shy, a stall where you throw balls at coconuts; the painted horses are those of a carousel.
explanation.definitionFit: Funfair sites hold coconut shies and merry-go-rounds with wooden horses, so these are the places for them.

clue.text: It goes pear-shaped for self-centred person

indicators.note: something that goes pear-shaped goes wrong and out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, doing double duty with the indicator

explanation.surface: Things turn out badly for someone who thinks only of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes pear-shaped' is British slang for going wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selfishly focused on their own interests is called this, a near synonym of egotist.

clue.text: The territory above a taxman's scope

blocks.note: taken as written
IR, the Inland Revenue, Britain's former tax authority
scope and space both mean room to act

explanation.surface: A tax inspector's range of investigation reaching up over the land.
explanation.walkthrough: IR stood for the Inland Revenue, the British tax office before it merged into HMRC.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's sovereignty extends to the sky over its land, the zone aircraft must get permission to enter.

clue.text: In Nepal, it's a sacred language

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow, across the gap

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Nepal into it

explanation.surface: A holy tongue spoken in the Himalayan kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Indian tongue in which the Theravada Buddhist scriptures are written, hence holy.

clue.text: Records found before Ezra

blocks.note: first meaning: historical accounts
second meaning: the books of the Old Testament placed just ahead of the Book of Ezra

explanation.surface: Archives discovered predating a biblical scribe.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible's order, the two books of this name come immediately before Ezra.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical accounts set down in order of events are so called, and the Bible books bear that name.

clue.text: Big names in disarray: I cite rebels

indicators.note: disarray is disorder, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone accusing the famous of being rebellious and disorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous people are informally called big names, so the two terms are synonyms for stars.

clue.text: One big in the game, other than Pele

indicators.note: other suggests a different form, so the words that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A star of football, though not the great Brazilian himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is not football but big game, the large animals hunted on safari. Pele is the Brazilian football great.
explanation.definitionFit: Big game means the large wild animals hunted for sport, and this huge African mammal is one of them.

clue.text: Thin paint

blocks.note: first meaning: delicate and fragile like a bird's shell
second meaning: a type of paint finish with a slight sheen

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a watery coat of paint; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain is described as having this delicate quality, and decorators sell a low-sheen finish under the same name.

clue.text: Club magazine

blocks.note: first meaning: the London football team
second meaning: a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a fan's publication; 'magazine' is in fact an arms store. The football club is based in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in military use is a stockpile of weapons, and the Gunners football side takes its name from the Woolwich armoury.

clue.text: Surveys about attitudes

blocks.note: re means concerning
attitudes are opinions or views

explanation.surface: Opinion polls on what people think.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey something is to look it over critically, and such assessments or overviews are synonyms here.

clue.text: Where they might bring back the birch?

definitions.text: Where they might bring back the birch?

blocks.clueFragment: Where they might bring back the birch?
blocks.note: surface reading: a place keen to restore flogging with a birch rod as punishment
setter's reading: places that reintroduce or replant birch trees, as tree collections do

explanation.surface: A hardline place that would restore corporal punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back the birch' is a British rallying cry for reviving flogging; here the birch is simply a tree being replanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical gardens devoted to trees grow many species, so birch trees could well be planted again there.

clue.text: In chess, when to swop a queen isn't clear

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the adjective meaning not clear

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of swop through a into queen

explanation.surface: A chess player unsure when to trade off a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting is camouflage; the letters lie in plain sight across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be seen through, or a meaning hard to understand, is not transparent or plain.

clue.text: Set out to marry drunk

indicators.note: out suggests disorder or being put wrong, so the word before is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to a wedding already intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is informal slang for intoxicated, like pickled or sozzled.

clue.text: Colour: mostly green with a hint of yellow

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word's tail end is removed
a hint is a tiny trace, so just the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of yellow

explanation.surface: Describing a shade that is largely green tinged with yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final N from green, then add the first letter of yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral shade between black and white, one of the basic hues, so an example of a colour.

clue.text: Free kind of house?

blocks.note: first meaning: unattached, separated
second meaning: a house standing alone, not joined to its neighbours

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an advert for a house given away; British estate agents class homes as detached, semi-detached or terraced.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unattached or loosened is described this way, and a standalone home not sharing walls is one sort of dwelling.

clue.text: Exercising choice of imitation

indicators.note: exercising works something hard, putting the following letters through their paces into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Using one's right to choose by copying someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that mimic sounds, such as buzz or cuckoo, are called echoic, so the adjective concerns imitating.

clue.text: Slander male trapped in silly lunacy

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so the word after is jumbled
something trapped in another is held inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man caught up in foolish madness and smeared with lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A false and damaging statement about someone is defamation, and this formal word is a synonym for that.

clue.text: Colours moving slowly around Spain

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the word after is rearranged
around says the jumbled letters surround what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Paint shades creeping gradually across Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades of the hue of lemons and butter are examples of colours, plural noun matching plural.
